When the instrument is used for microscopy, the spectroradiometer and the microscope are coupled through the fiber optic accessory. The interchangeable 0.5, 1, and 2 degree fields of view belong to the spectroradiometer lens and are used in non-microscopy applications, at the working distances stated in the answer to Q1. Q3. Does the imaging optic need to be mounted inside the microscope system, or outside of it looking through a window? A. The imaging optic is not mounted inside the microscope system. Coupling to the microscope is accomplished through the fiber optic accessory. Q4. The Statement of Work states a maximum probe dimension of 0.125 inches. Does that limit apply to the imaging optic itself, or only to the fiber probe? A. The 0.125 inch dimensional limit applies only to the fiber probe. It does not apply to the imaging optic. The fire precaution levels restrict certain forest operations as the fire danger increases. It is the responsibility of the individual operating on forest land to know the precaution level for the day and take the correct fire precautions. There are no precaution levels prior to the closed fire season. Each fire precaution level requires adherence to the restrictions applicable to all lower levels in addition to the limits placed by that level. Level 1 is the lowest level of fire danger usually occurring early in the season and perhaps again after significant rainfall during the season. All requirements listed above apply. Rather than focusing solely on utilization-based programs, the HPO model prioritizes a performance-oriented strategy that integrates strength and conditioning, nutrition, mental resilience, and recovery protocols. This transformation will require restructuring organizational roles, updating training standards, and implementing standardized operating procedures to ensure consistent quality across all programs. The expected outcome of this transition is enhanced readiness and well-being, achieved by adopting multidisciplinary practices. Implementation will involve strategic staff development, updated certification requirements, and role adjustments to support a smooth transition. The initial implementation phase will utilize current resources and Program of Record (POR) allocations at selected installations, providing insight into broader rollout and future resource planning. The successful adoption of the HPO model will modernize Navy performance and resiliency programming, aligning with best practices in human performance optimization. certifications_partner.text: irectorate with current national commercial medical/surgical supplies and pharmaceutical sales data. IQVIA is the only source that offers a sales data and analytics data subscription license that tracks national and commercial medical/surgical and pharmaceutical sales data. The IQVIA data license subscription for medical/surgical and pharmaceutical sales data provides critical data feeds necessary for the DMLSS-W application, including a tool to track medical/pharmaceutical usage, retail and wholesale prices, and sales trends. IQVIA’s data collection processes, results, editing, and filtering processes are proprietary and there are no authorized resellers or alternative sources of supply. The DMLSS-W system relies on and incorporates IQVIA data and uses it on a daily basis. The IQVIA Medical Device and Supply Audit (MDSA) component of the data package measures sales data of medical devices and supplies sold and acquired by U.S. hospitals. The MDSA component provides purchase details for approximately five-hundred-fifty-thousand (550,000) stock keeping units (SKUs) used for tracking inventory and sales of nearly three-thousand (3,000) medical supply manufacturers and industry participants selling products to U.S. hospitals. The IQVIA Pharmaceutical Sales Data, Relational Data Model for

medical supply manufacturers and industry participants selling products to U.S. hospitals. The IQVIA Pharmaceutical Sales Data, Relational Data Model for Pharmaceutical Sales Data, Medical/Surgical Sales Data, Relational Data Model for Medical/Surgical Sales Data, Medical/Surgical Synonym File, and Package Allocation for Medical/Surgical Data is supplied to Government and commercial entities under a monthly subscription, , while the Comprehensive Data Dictionary is supplied under the license is distributed on an annual basis. Market research was conducted by contacting IQVIA directly to obtain a budgetary quote. IQVIA currently has no authorized resellers and is therefore the only source for the data license subscription. Use of this brand name license in the acquisition is essential to the Government’s requirement, thereby precluding consideration of a product from another provider. The IQVIA data license subscription is particular to one manufacturer, IQVIA, and any resultant acquisition cannot not be fulfilled under full and open competition due to the absence of authorized resellers for IQVIA and its products, and no other type of supply or service will satisfy the Government’s need. 5. The contractor shall distribute SOC reports and Bridge Letters to stakeholders within five business days of receipt. The contractor shall maintain a SOC Reports and Bridge Letters Tracker of all reports expected to be received and update the government lead immediately when any reports or bridge letters are not received by expected deadlines. SCOPE OR MISSION : The mission of NOAA CSL is to conduct scientific research aimed at discovering, understanding, and quantifying the processes that govern the chemical reactions of Earth’s atmosphere that are needed to improve the capability to predict its behavior. BACKGROUND: The software within the LabView Enterprise Agreement Service ID EA-15701

mical reactions of Earth’s atmosphere that are needed to improve the capability to predict its behavior. BACKGROUND: The software within the LabView Enterprise Agreement Service ID EA-15701 has been used to develop various CSL instrumentation and other CSL hardware systems. Only NI specific software drivers can be used with these hardware systems. From this system, thousands of programs have been developed to not only run the instruments but also analyze data from them using LabView software. TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS: The contractor shall provide for all entitlements provided under Enterprise Agreement Service ID EA-15701. SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS: This requirement is restricted to brand-name LabView by NI only. The Connect Program (Wyman et al 2020; 2022) provides group interactive training for military personnel, followed by text messages and base-wide activities to embed concepts into culture and peer networks. The Connect Program’s interactive group design progresses from individual engagement (e.g., each participant shares career goals and values) to building group-level skills and norms (e.g., mapping group strengths). n Foreign Procurements-Notice and Representation (Jun 2020) (a) Deﬁnitions. As used in this provision- Foreign person means any person other than a United States person. Speciﬁed Federal procurement payment means any payment made pursuant to a contract with a foreign contracting party that is for goods, manufactured or produced, or services provided in a foreign country that is not a party to an international procurement agreement with the United States. For purposes of the prior sentence, a foreign country does not include an outlying area of the United States. United States person as deﬁned in 26 U.S.C. 7701(a)(30) means (1) A citizen or resident of the United States; (2) A domestic partnership; (3) A domestic corporation; (4) Any estate (other than a foreign estate, within the meaning of 26 U.S.C. 701(a)(31)); and (5) Any trust if- (i) A court within the United States is able to exercise primary supervision over the administration of the trust; and (ii) One or more United States persons have the authority to control all substantial decisions of the trust. (b) Unless exempted, there is a 2 percent tax of the amount of a speciﬁed Federal procurement payment on any foreign person receiving such payment. See 26 U.S.C. 5000C and its implementing regulations at 26 CFR 1.5000C-1 through 1

references_experience.text: CMC will review submitted white papers in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified in the Call. If a vendor’s white paper is evaluated favorably by AFLCMC, the Government will send initially selected vendors a Request for Proposal (RFP). Invited vendors will proceed to preparing and submitting a proposal for evaluation. Additional details will be included within the RFP. Incorporate Sections 6.1.2-6.1.4 After the submission of the white papers and issuance of RFPs to favorably evaluated white papers, the remaining process is the same as the one-step, closed Call. Therefore, Sections 6.1.2, 6.1.3 and 6.1.4 are hereby incorporated by Reference. Open Period Calls This CSO may have Open Period Calls that consist only of a two-step process. For this Call type, the process will mirror the process articulated in 6.2 above; however, with the important distinction that white papers will be accepted at any time during the stated time period on the Call. This is in contrast to a Closed Call where all proposals are required to be submitted at a specific date and time together and follow a standard timeline for all participants. For Open Period Calls, the timelines are usually less structured and broader in nature. Typical turn-around times that Vendors can expect are usually stated in the

ct to the restriction on the title page of this proposal. Classified Proposals Classified whitepapers/proposals will not be accepted under this CSO unless otherwise stated in the Call. If topics require classified work, the proposing vendor must have a facility clearance in order to perform the work. Security Security classification will be determined for each Call/Award. If classified data will be accessed or generated, a facility and storage clearance, at the required classification level, will be required and the proposal will discuss appropriate personnel and facility clearances. If a vendor has any reason to believe their concept may reference ideas or operations that require special protection, the vendor should immediately contact the Contracting/Agreements Officer for further instruction. Additionally, if a DD254 is applicable for a Call/Award, vendors must verify their Cognizant Security Office information is current with Defense Security Service (DSS). Promotional Material Promotional and non-project related discussion is discouraged, and additional information provided via Universal Resource Locator (URL) links or on computer disks, CDs, DVDs, video tapes or any other medium will not be accepted or considered in the proposal evaluation unless otherwise directed by the Call

The standard provides four increasing, qualitative levels of security intended to cover a wide range of potential applications and environments. The security requirements cover areas related to the secure design, implementation, and operation of a cryptographic module. These areas include cryptographic module specification; cryptographic module interfaces; roles, services, and authentication; software/firmware security; operating environment; physical security; non-invasive security; sensitive security parameter management; self-tests; life-cycle assurance; and mitigation of other attacks. This CSO authority is established under section 803 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2022 (Pub. L. 117-81) and Class Deviation 2022-O0007. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC) programs require the utilization and leveraging of the latest technology advances from a large variety of prospective Contractors. AFLCMC invites innovating technical approach proposals addressing all aspects of DataOps focusing on the below objective areas. However, these enumerated focus areas are minimum requirements, and AFLCMC is open to the identification of technologies useful for modernizing DataOps for sophisticated security and weapon systems. This requires delivering an enduring, secure, robust, efficient, responsive, agile, elastic, and extensible classified DataOps solution. This CSO will focus on existing and emerging technologies and platforms across AFLCMC, Department of the Air Force (DAF), Department of Defense (DoD) and the Intelligence Community, as well as leveraging commercial markets to perform an integrated analysis of the capabilities of varying technologies that support our critical national security systems and prioritize investme

Government reserves the right to issue separate Calls for each DataOps Focus Area or combine several Focus Areas under an individual Call. Disclaimer: No proposals or white papers are being requested at this time. Those will be requested via Calls published under the CSO solicitation. AFLCMC is not obligated to make any awards from any publicized Call, and all awards under this CSO are explicitly subject to the availability of funds and successful negotiations. The Government is not responsible for any monies expended by any vendor prior to the issuance of any awarded contract/agreement. AFLCMC reserves the right to modify the solicitation requirements of this CSO and each subsequent Call at its sole discretion. This CSO seeks to fund innovative technologies that propose new solutions to expand AFLCMC’s capabilities as it relates to modern DataOps Focus Areas. AFLCMC is interested in capabilities from all interested vendors to include, but not limited to, traditional defense contractors, nontraditional defense contractors, large businesses, small businesses, and research institutions (collectively referred as vendors). It should be noted, many of the critical national security systems operate in varying classification environments, including highly classified environments – such as collate

ve solutions that vendors can bring forth to meet the stated Areas of Interest detailed in each Call. DataOps Technology Focus Areas AFLCMC is seeking capabilities to prove out end-to-end DataOps for representative modern embedded weapon systems. The desired end-state is a DataOps capability/prototype that enables a weapon system to exploit data across the full lifecycle of an embedded weapon system (development, integration, test, deployment, operations and sustainment) across all classification levels. An ideal partner has first-party ability to directly modify underlying commercial hyperscale and edge cloud fabric to meet the project’s requirements across all classification levels and supporting partners would be considered as enabling providers supporting specific aspects of the potential solution. Each Technology Focus Area identifies an area where prospective vendors can bring substantial value to meet the DataOps mission. These focus areas are meant to be read expansively and are not limited to the enumerated Focus Areas. Additional Focus Areas may be included via amendments to this CSO. Software-Defined Networking (SDN) AFLCMC has a requirement to explore implementing SDN for fully networked Command, Control and Communications (C3) functionality, particularly in day-to-day Military Operating Base (MOB) and sustainment missions. SDN should contain a high degree of network programmability and reconfigurability to meet the needs of different government systems and emphasize advantageous situational awareness for faster response times. Further, AFLCMC is interested in other ways SDN can be applied to military environments while preserving data security. Edge Hyper-Converged Infrastructure AFLCMC anticipates migrating away from discrete, hardware-defined systems toward software-defined environments permitting all functionality through commercial service platforms while protecting data at all classification levels (unclassified, secret, top secret, SAP). FIPS 140.3 is the standard that shall be used in designing and implementing cryptographic modules that federal departments and agencies operate or are operated for them under contract. The standard provides four increasing, qualitative levels of security intended to cover a wide range of potential applications and environments. The security requirements cover areas related to the secure design, implementation, and operation of a cryptographic module. These areas include cryptographic module specification; cryptographic module interfaces; roles, services, and authentication; software/firmware security; operating environment; physical security; non-invasive security; sensitive security parameter management; self-tests; life-cycle assurance; and mitigation of other attacks. Organizations with familiarization and expertise with establishing and maintaining compliant data encryption could be of use to the DoD. Purpose The Federal Retirement Thrift Investment Board (FRTIB), Office of General Counsel (OGC), is conducting market research to identify commercially available products, services, and solution approaches that support Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) processing, eDiscovery, Matter Management, and related legal operations functions. Information obtained through this Request for Information (RFI) will be used to better understand current market capabilities, validate and refine agency requirements, and support acquisition planning. This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. FRTIB welcomes responses from vendors offering: An integrated platform addressing multiple functional areas; Modular or interoperable solutions that collectively provide the desired capabilities; or Standalone products or services that address specific FOIA, eDiscovery, Matter Management, reporting, or knowledge-management needs. For purposes of this RFI, interoperable solutions are those that enable efficient exchange and synchronization of records, metadata, case information, workflow status, and related content with minimal manual intervention while maintaining appropriate security, audit, and records management controls. Proposed solutions should demonstrate how they support one or more of the following capability areas. 4.1 FOIA Management FRTIB is interested in capabilities supporting: Centralized intake and creation of FOIA cases; Case tracking and lifecycle management; Workflow management and task assignment; Deadline monitoring and statutory compliance tracking; Automated notifications and escalation management; Search and collection of responsive records; Document review and collaboration; Native-format redaction and exemption management; Production package creation; Correspondence management; Reporting and FOIA performance metrics; and Audit trails supporting legal defensibility. 4.2 eDiscovery and Records Collection FRTIB is interested in capabilities supporting: Defensible search and records collection; Search across Microsoft 365 and other enterprise data sources; Custodian and non-custodian collection workflows; Legal holds and preservation activit

service capabilities. eDiscovery capabilities should be capable of supporting legal, investigative, records management, and other non-FOIA use cases independent of FOIA operations while preferably maintaining integration with any proposed FOIA solution. FRTIB is particularly interested in solutions that provide an intuitive and integrated interface for search, collection, review, and management activities, reducing reliance on multiple administrative tools and complex workflows. 4.3 Matter Management FRTIB is interested in Matter Management capabilities supporting: Matter intake and creation; Configurable matter types and workflows; Task and deadline management; Document and correspondence management; Collaboration among attorneys and business stakeholders; Relationship mapping among matters, people, documents, and records; Workload management; Reporting and performance metrics; Role-based access controls; and Integration with Microsoft 365 applications and services. 4.4 Knowledge Management FRTIB is interested in capabilities that facilitate the identification, organization, retention, and reuse of institutional knowledge, including: Matter-to-matter relationship tracking; Precedent and work product reuse; Search across historical matters and documents; Identification of recurring legal
